<thought>We need a SMILES whose molecular formula is C4H7N3O (neutral mass ≈ 113.060 Da). The heterocycle 1,2,4‑oxadiazole (C2H2N2O) with an N‑methyl substituent adds one carbon and three hydrogens, giving C3H5N3O. Adding one more carbon (as a methyl group attached to the carbon of the ring) yields C4H7N3O. The SMILES “CN1N=COC1” represents N‑methyl‑1,2,4‑oxadiazole, which has formula C3H5N3O, so it is still short one carbon. A better candidate is “C1=NN(C)C(=O)O1” (a 5‑membered ring containing N,N,O with a carbonyl and a methyl substituent). I will test the SMILES “C1=NN(C)C(=O)O1” to see its formula.</thought>
